findings.title: GitHub user check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: When no Integration row exists for `installation_id`, the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch returns `pipeline.next_step()` before the new authenticated-user check (lines 501-505) runs. That check only executes when an Integration already exists with `metadata["sender"]`, which the installation webhook normally creates. The webhook is delivered asynchronously while the browser is redirected back to Sentry, so if the browser returns first, or the webhook is delayed or dropped, the pipeline completes without verifying that the authenticated GitHub user is the one who installed the app. This fail-open path defeats the guarantee the PR describes. The check should fail closed when there is no installer record to compare against, or the installer identity should be obtained another way.

findings.title: KeyError when an existing Integration has no sender metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError if the Integration row has no `sender` key. `build_integration` only writes `sender` when the pipeline state contains one (lines 376-377), and integrations created by the pipeline without a webhook do not have it (test_basic_flow asserts metadata with no sender). This line is reached for any Integration row that exists without an OrganizationIntegration, so the install flow returns a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and return `error(...)` when the sender is missing.

findings.title: Installer check compares mutable GitHub logins instead of immutable user IDs
findings.body: The check compares `login` strings. GitHub usernames can be renamed, and the old name then becomes claimable by another account. The webhook `sender` payload and the `/user` response both include the numeric `id`, which is immutable. If the installer renames their account and another user claims the old login, that second account would pass this check. Comparing `id` values would close this gap.

findings.title: Integration lookups for the security check are not scoped by provider
findings.body: The lookups at lines 478 and 494-496 filter only on `external_id` and not on `provider`. `external_id` is unique only per provider, so `get` can raise an unhandled MultipleObjectsReturned (500), or it can return a non-GitHub row whose metadata is then used for the sender comparison at line 503. The lookup used for the security decision should include `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`.

findings.title: Network and API failures during token exchange and user lookup are not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 and `get_user_info` at line 434 are not wrapped in error handling, unlike the body parsing at lines 425-429. A connection failure, timeout, or non-2xx response from GitHub propagates out of the view and produces a 500 instead of the failure page that the rest of this view renders. These calls should be wrapped so the view returns `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

findings.title: Installation now hard-requires GitHub OAuth client credentials
findings.body: The new step reads the GitHub OAuth client ID and secret (lines 394-395) and places the client ID into the authorize URL without checking that it is set. On deployments that have the GitHub App configured but not GitHub login OAuth credentials, the authorize URL contains `client_id=None`, so users are sent to a GitHub error page and cannot install the integration. This new requirement is not mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: No test for the success path of the new installer check or for the skipped-check path
findings.body: The only test exercising the new check (`test_github_user_mismatch`) covers the failure case. Nothing verifies that a webhook-created Integration whose `sender` matches the OAuth user completes the pipeline. Nothing covers an installation with no Integration row yet, which is the path where the check is skipped entirely (see the fail-open finding in integration.py). Both cases need tests.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the not-found path
findings.body: The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' was removed. The test now sends a mismatched state, which fails at the state check before `build_integration` runs. The `IntegrationError` raised on a GitHub API 404 (integration.py lines 352-357) is therefore untested, and the `responses.replace(... status=404)` mock is never hit. Restore coverage by sending a matching state, or keep the original test.
